title: Can right ventricular endomyocardial biopsy predict left ventricular fibrosis beforehand in dilated cardiomyopathy?
study_context: Paired DCM pathology study of 70 patients: earlier RV biopsies and subsequent whole-heart material, including 52 explanted native hearts and 18 autopsy hearts.
population_or_data: Paired DCM pathology study of 70 patients: earlier RV biopsies and subsequent whole-heart material, including 52 explanted native hearts and 18 autopsy hearts.
task: Paired DCM pathology study of 70 patients: earlier RV biopsies and subsequent whole-heart material, including 52 explanted native hearts and 18 autopsy hearts.
method: Image-based fibrosis-area measurement in biopsy and larger-heart sections, with analysis accounting for biopsy-to-excision interval.
main_findings: The study compared earlier right-ventricular biopsy fibrosis with later whole-heart fibrosis in the same patients, combining 52 explant and 18 autopsy cases; biopsy-to-excision time was explicitly considered.
limitations: Selected-page review, not full-paper audit. PDF pages 1, 2 and extracted text visually checked on 2026-10-07.

DCM native-heart fibrosis is not rejection in a transplanted heart. Explant and autopsy are different specimen origins. Not AI transfer, not proof of stable pathology across the intervening years, and no rejection-performance benefit follows.
does_not_establish: DCM native-heart fibrosis is not rejection in a transplanted heart. Explant and autopsy are different specimen origins. Not AI transfer, not proof of stable pathology across the intervening years, and no rejection-performance benefit follows.
relevance_to_project: A concrete matched-patient design for connecting small biopsies to larger cardiac specimens while retaining chronology.
